banana.name_note: Several species are grown; the genus is used.

broccoli.name_note: Crop variety of Brassica oleracea L.; GBIF treats the varieties as part of that species.

cabbage.name_note: Crop variety of Brassica oleracea L.; GBIF treats the varieties as part of that species.

carrot.name_note: Cultivated carrot is Daucus carota subsp. sativus.

cauliflower.name_note: Crop variety of Brassica oleracea L.; GBIF treats the varieties as part of that species.

citrus.name_note: Several species are grown; the genus is used.

maple.name_note: Several species are grown; the genus is used.

squash.name_note: Several species are grown; the genus is used.

conditions.name: Black rot
conditions.symptoms: Purple flecks on leaves that become round spots with brown centers and purple edges ('frogeye'). Fruit gets firm brown rot with black and brown rings and may shrivel into mummies that stay on the tree.
look_for: Round leaf spots with brown centers and purple edges?
Shriveled, mummified fruit still on the tree?
management: Remove dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit; burn prunings.
Plant disease-free seedlings in well-drained soil.

conditions.name: Apple mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Cream to yellow spots, blotches, bands or vein patterns on the upper side of leaves; yield loss is usually slight.
look_for: Bright cream or yellow patterns on the leaves?
Fruit looks normal?
management: Buy virus-tested trees from reputable nurseries.
Do not take graftwood from infected trees.
No chemical treatment works; remove badly affected trees if needed.

conditions.name: Cedar apple rust
conditions.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf with tiny black dots in the center and a red band around them; later, small cup-like structures form under the leaf. The fungus needs nearby cedar (juniper) trees.
look_for: Bright orange-yellow spots with tiny black dots?
Cedar or juniper trees growing nearby?
management: Plant resistant varieties.
Avoid planting near cedar trees, or remove nearby cedars.
Plant clean seedlings from reliable sources.

conditions.name: Apple scab
conditions.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots with uneven edges on leaves and fruit; fruit spots become dark, rough and corky, and badly infected leaves yellow and drop.
look_for: Olive-green velvety spots on leaves?
Dark, rough, corky spots on the fruit?
management: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves.
Prune to keep an open canopy and space trees properly.
Plant disease-free seedlings from certified nurseries.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
conditions.symptoms: Brown to black spots on the fruit peel that grow into large dark sunken areas, especially on ripening fruit.
look_for: Dark sunken spots on the fruit peel?
Spots growing as the fruit ripens?
management: Avoid injuring the fruit during harvest and handling.
Remove old flower parts that can carry the fungus.

conditions.name: Black leaf streak (black Sigatoka)
conditions.symptoms: Small red-brown streaks along the veins on young leaves that become dark spots with gray centers, black edges and yellow halos; large parts of the leaf die and bunches ripen unevenly.
look_for: Red-brown streaks running along the leaf veins?
Dark spots with yellow halos on older leaves?
management: Plant disease-free, tolerant planting material.
Space plants, control weeds and remove extra suckers so leaves dry quickly.
Remove leaves with mature spots.
Act as soon as the first symptoms appear, especially in humid weather.

conditions.name: Bunchy top
conditions.symptoms: Each new leaf is smaller and stands upright in a bunch at the top; leaf edges are pale and wavy, with dark-green 'dot-dash' streaks along the veins. Spread by aphids.
look_for: New leaves small and bunched upright at the top?
Dark-green dot-dash streaks along the veins?
management: Use disease-free planting material from a registered nursery.
Do not bring planting material from affected areas.
Control aphids and keep fields weed-free.
Uproot and destroy infected plants.

conditions.name: Cigar end rot
conditions.symptoms: The tips of the fingers darken, wrinkle and rot; the rotted tip may dry out or be covered with gray-white spores, like the ash of a cigar.
look_for: Finger tips dark and rotted?
Gray, ash-like covering on the rotted tips?
management: Remove dead flower parts from the bunch.
Cover bunches with perforated plastic bags.

sources.title: Ugonjwa wa kuchomeka vidole vya ndizi (Cigar end rot)

conditions.name: Cordana leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Oval pale brown spots near the leaf edges on lower leaves, with rings inside and a yellow halo; spots can merge into large dead areas.
look_for: Oval brown spots near the leaf edge?
Rings inside the spots with a yellow halo?
management: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
If severe, ask a technician about a copper-based fungicide.

conditions.name: Panama disease (Fusarium wilt)
conditions.name_note: Forma specialis of Fusarium oxysporum; GBIF does not list formae speciales separately.
conditions.symptoms: Older leaves turn yellow and wilt, leaf sheaths split and the whole canopy dies. Inside the pseudostem and rhizome, the vascular tissue is reddish brown.
look_for: Older leaves yellowing and wilting from the edges?
Reddish-brown streaks inside when the pseudostem is cut?
management: There is no cure once a plant is infected.
Plant only disease-free planting material.
The fungus spreads in soil, running water and infected rhizomes, so keep these from moving out of infected areas.

sources.title: Mnyauko fusari (Fusarium wilt or Panama disease) wa migomba

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.symptoms: Leaves yellow, often starting along the middle vein, with gray fuzzy growth underneath; brown-black angular patches follow.
look_for: Gray fuzzy growth under the leaves?
Yellowing that starts along the middle vein?
management: Grow tolerant varieties.
Keep air moving around plants and water with drip lines to keep leaves dry.

conditions.name: Halo blight
conditions.name_note: Pathovar name used in plant pathology; GBIF does not list pathovars separately.
conditions.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots under the leaf that turn brown, surrounded by a wide yellow-green halo; pods get red-brown greasy spots.
look_for: Wide yellow halo around small brown spots?
Greasy spots on the pods?
management: Plant disease-free seed.
Rotate to non-host crops every two years and plow bean debris under.

conditions.name: Bean common mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling, downward curling or cupping of leaves, and deformed pods; plants from infected seed are stunted. Spread by seed and aphids.
look_for: Mottled leaves that curl down or cup?
Stunted plants with misshapen pods?
management: Use certified disease-free seed.
Plant resistant varieties.
Controlling aphids may slow spread; there is no chemical cure.

conditions.name: Bean rust
conditions.symptoms: Small yellow-white spots that become raised brick-red pustules, often with a yellow halo; leaves may drop early.
look_for: Raised brick-red pustules?
Reddish powder that rubs off?
management: Grow resistant varieties.
Remove infected debris, rotate crops and control weeds.

conditions.name: Bacterial spot
conditions.symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaf undersides that dry and turn brown; raised brown cankers on stems and cracked brown spots on fruit.
look_for: Water-soaked spots that turn brown?
Rough, cracked spots on the fruit?
management: Use disease-free seed and transplants.
Remove crop debris after harvest or plow it deeply under.

conditions.name: Blossom end rot
conditions.symptoms: A water-soaked spot at the blossom end of the fruit that becomes sunken, tan and leathery. It is not an infection: it comes from low calcium in the fruit, often caused by uneven watering.
look_for: Sunken leathery patch at the bottom (blossom end) of the fruit?
Leaves otherwise healthy?
management: Water evenly and mulch to keep soil moisture steady.
Keep soil pH near 6.5; lime if needed.
Avoid ammonium fertilizers and over-fertilizing.

conditions.name: Frogeye leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small round spots with white to brown centers and a dark red-purple border, like a frog's eye; old spots crack in the middle.
look_for: Round spots with light centers and dark borders?
Spot centers brittle or cracked?
management: Remove crop debris after harvest.
Rotate crops.

sources.title: Cercospora leaf spot (Frogeye leaf spot) (pepper bell)

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.symptoms: White powdery patches on the underside of leaves with yellow to brown areas on top; leaf edges curl up and leaves may drop.
look_for: White powder under the leaves?
Yellow patches on the upper side?
management: Ask a technician about a fungicide if the disease is severe.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
conditions.symptoms: Usually hidden until ripening: ripe berries soften and shrivel near the blossom end and ooze small orange spore masses. Twig blight and leaf spots can also occur.
look_for: Ripe berries soft and shriveled at the blossom end?
Orange, slimy spore masses on the fruit?
management: Plant less susceptible varieties.
Prune for air flow and shorten leaf wetness with drip irrigation.
Cool and handle harvested fruit quickly.

sources.title: Michigan Blueberry Facts: Anthracnose Fruit Rot (E3039)

conditions.name: Botrytis blight (gray mold)
conditions.symptoms: Open blossoms turn brown and blighted and do not set fruit; leaves touching infected blossoms get brown spots. Gray mold may cover affected parts.
look_for: Brown, blighted blossoms?
Gray fuzzy mold on flowers or fruit?
management: Protect flowers at mid-bloom and late bloom when the disease is a problem.

conditions.name: Mummy berry
conditions.symptoms: New shoots and leaves suddenly droop and brown in spring; infected berries turn cream or pink, then tan or gray, and shrivel into hard mummies.
look_for: New shoots wilting and browning in spring?
Berries shriveled into hard, gray mummies?
management: Plant disease-free plants.
Remove mummified berries or bury them under at least 2.5 cm of soil.

conditions.name: Leaf rust
conditions.name_note: Formerly Thekopsora minima (NSW DPI); Pucciniastrum vaccinii in western North America.
conditions.symptoms: Small angular yellow spots on the upper leaf that turn red to black, with yellow-orange powdery pustules underneath; badly infected bushes lose leaves early. Worse near hemlock trees.
look_for: Yellow-orange powder under the leaves?
Yellow spots turning red-brown on top?
management: Choose more resistant varieties.
Scout regularly and remove nearby hemlocks where practical.

conditions.name: Blueberry scorch
conditions.symptoms: Flowers and leaves suddenly die and blight in spring on sensitive varieties; other varieties show no symptoms. Spread by aphids and takes 1-2 years to show.
look_for: Flowers and new leaves dying suddenly at bloom?
Whole bush or branches affected, not single leaves?
management: Plant virus-tested stock and test bushes with symptoms.
Remove and destroy infected plants and control aphids.
Clean harvesting equipment.

sources.title: Managing blueberry viruses in the Pacific Northwest (EM 9518)

conditions.name: Alternaria leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small dark spots that turn brown to gray, often with rings and a purple-black edge; the centers can crack. Dark streaks may form on stems.
look_for: Brown-gray spots with rings?
Dark purple-black edge around the spots?
management: Plant only clean seed.
Rotate away from cabbage-family crops.

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.gbif: Hyaloperonospora brassicae (Gäum.) Göker, Voglmayr, Riethm., Weiss & Oberw.
conditions.symptoms: Small angular yellow patches on the upper leaf that turn brown, with white fluffy growth underneath.
look_for: White fluffy growth under the leaf?
Angular yellow patches on top?
management: Remove crop debris after harvest.
Rotate with non-cabbage-family crops.

conditions.name: Ring spot
conditions.symptoms: Small purple spots with a water-soaked ring that become brown spots 1-2 cm across with olive-green borders, often with rings of tiny black dots.
look_for: Round brown spots with many tiny black dots in rings?
Olive-green border around the spots?
management: Avoid fields that had the disease before.
Rotate with non-cabbage-family crops and clean tools regularly.

conditions.name: Alternaria leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small dark spots that turn brown to gray, often with rings and a purple-black edge; the centers can crack.
look_for: Brown-gray spots with rings?
Dark purple-black edge around the spots?
management: Plant only clean seed.
Rotate away from cabbage-family crops.

sources.title: Alternaria leaf spot (Black spot, Gray spot) (kale)

conditions.name: Black rot
conditions.symptoms: Yellow to brown V-shaped patches that start at the leaf edge and point toward the midrib; veins and stems turn black.
look_for: V-shaped yellow-brown patches starting at the leaf edge?
Blackened veins?
management: Plant clean seed and resistant varieties.
Rotate away from cabbage-family crops for two years.
Remove cabbage-family weeds and keep the field clean.

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.gbif: Hyaloperonospora brassicae (Gäum.) Göker, Voglmayr, Riethm., Weiss & Oberw.
conditions.symptoms: Irregular yellow patches on leaves that turn light brown, with fluffy gray growth underneath.
look_for: Fluffy gray growth under the leaf?
Yellow patches on top of the leaf?
management: Remove crop debris after harvest.
Rotate with non-cabbage-family crops.

conditions.name: Alternaria leaf blight
conditions.symptoms: Green-brown water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown to black and merge, so leaves yellow and die.
look_for: Dark brown to black spots on leaf edges?
Leaves dying from the tips?
management: Treat seed with hot water before planting.
Act early in warm, wet weather.

conditions.name: Cavity spot
conditions.name_note: GBIF accepts Globisporangium violae; older literature uses Pythium violae.
conditions.gbif: Globisporangium violae (Chesters & Hickman) Uzuhashi, Tojo & Kakish.
conditions.symptoms: Sunken, oval gray spots across the root; the skin breaks and dark elongated lesions with small cracks form.
look_for: Small sunken oval spots across the root?
Leaves look normal?
management: Avoid fields where cavity spot occurred before.
Do not over-fertilize.

conditions.name: Cercospora leaf blight
conditions.symptoms: Small dead flecks with yellow halos that grow into tan-brown spots; leaves wither, curl and die.
look_for: Small tan spots with yellow halos?
Leaves curling and drying?
management: Plant clean seed and rotate crops.
Plow crop debris under after harvest.

conditions.name: Alternaria leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small dark spots that turn brown to gray, often with rings and a purple-black edge; the centers can crack.
look_for: Brown-gray spots with rings?
Dark purple-black edge around the spots?
management: Plant only clean seed.
Rotate away from cabbage-family crops.

conditions.name: Bacterial soft rot
conditions.symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves and curds that grow into a soft, rotten mass oozing slimy liquid that darkens in air.
look_for: Soft, slimy rot?
Bad smell from the rotting area?
management: No chemical treatment works; rely on good practices.
Plant in well-drained soil or raised beds and rotate crops.
Harvest heads only when dry and avoid damaging them.

conditions.name: Anthracnose (leaf curl)
conditions.symptoms: Leaves cup downward (leaf curl) and stay pale green; stalks get brown lesions and crowns may rot. Spread by splashing water in long wet, warm periods.
look_for: Leaves cupping downward?
Brown lesions on the stalks?
management: Hot-water treat seed and clean transplant trays.
Scout regularly and remove suspect plants.
Avoid overhead irrigation and control weed hosts.

conditions.name: Early blight
conditions.symptoms: Small yellow flecks that grow into brown-gray papery spots without clear borders; heavily spotted leaves die.
look_for: Brown-gray papery spots?
Spots without a clear border?
management: Plant clean seed and tolerant varieties.
Rotate crops and avoid crowding plants.

sources.title: Early blight (Cercospora leaf spot, Cercospora blight) (celery)

conditions.name: Cherry leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small purple or red spots on the upper leaf that turn brown; infected leaves yellow and drop early, weakening the tree.
look_for: Many small purple-red spots on the leaves?
Leaves yellowing and dropping in mid-season?
management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves to reduce spring infection.
Protect new leaves from petal fall on trees with a history of the disease.

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.name_note: Recently renamed Podosphaera cerasi; P. clandestina is still widely used (WSU).
conditions.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and shoots; leaves curl upward and new leaves stay pale and distorted. Fruit can be deformed.
look_for: White powder on leaves and young shoots?
Leaves curling upward?
management: Prune for air flow and remove infected water sprouts.
Plant resistant varieties; protect from petal fall in high-risk years.

sources.title: Powdery Mildew of Cherry and Plum in Home Fruit Plantings

conditions.name: Citrus canker
conditions.name_note: Marked doubtful in GBIF; this is the name used in current citrus canker literature.
conditions.symptoms: Raised corky spots with yellow halos on leaves (often at the edge or tip), twigs and fruit; old spots collapse into brown craters.
look_for: Raised, rough spots with yellow halos?
Spots on both leaves and fruit?
management: Where the disease is new, remove and destroy infected trees.
Use windbreaks and control leaf miners.
Copper sprays help where the disease is established.

conditions.name: Huanglongbing (citrus greening)
conditions.name_note: Candidatus (not yet cultured) bacteria are not in the GBIF backbone.
conditions.symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling that is not the same on both sides of the leaf vein, yellow shoots on one limb, and twig dieback. Fruit is small, lopsided, partly green and bitter. Spread by the citrus psyllid.
look_for: Blotchy yellow mottling not matching on both sides of the midrib?
Small lopsided fruit that stays partly green?
management: There is no cure; infected trees must be removed.
Plant only disease-free seedlings from a certified nursery.
Remove other host plants of the citrus psyllid near the farm and space trees well.
Follow quarantine rules on moving citrus plants.

conditions.name: Berry blotch
conditions.name_note: GBIF lists it under Cercosporina; plant pathology literature uses Cercospora coffeicola. Expert check advised.
conditions.symptoms: Brown sunken spots on green berries, sometimes with a purple halo; red berries can get large black sunken areas. Leaves may have the same disease as brown eye spot.
look_for: Brown sunken spots on green berries?
Round leaf spots with gray-white centers?
management: Fertilize adequately; weak plants are more susceptible.
Remove debris after pruning.
Space and prune plants to open the canopy.

sources.title: Cercospora leaf spot (Brown eye spot, Berry blotch) (coffee)

conditions.name: Black rot (thread blight)
conditions.name_note: GBIF accepts Rhizoctonia noxia; coffee literature often uses older names.
conditions.gbif: Rhizoctonia noxia (Donk) Oberw., R.Bauer, Garnica & R.Kirschner
conditions.symptoms: Light-colored threads and mats grow on the underside of leaves and twigs; leaves turn gray, dry, then black and fall, followed by twig dieback.
look_for: Thread-like white or light growth on twigs and leaf undersides?
Blackened dead leaves hanging from threads?
management: Prune affected branches about 30 cm below the affected part.
Combine cultural, biological and chemical measures as advised locally.

conditions.name: Brown eye spot
conditions.name_note: GBIF lists it under Cercosporina; plant pathology literature uses Cercospora coffeicola. Expert check advised.
conditions.symptoms: Round brown leaf spots that develop gray-white centers with a red-brown edge, like an eye, sometimes with a yellow halo; leaves may drop early.
look_for: Round spots with gray-white centers and red-brown edges?
Leaves dropping early?
management: Fertilize adequately; weak plants are more susceptible.
Remove debris after pruning.
Space and prune plants to open the canopy.

sources.title: Cercospora leaf spot (Brown eye spot, Berry blotch) (coffee)

conditions.name: Coffee leaf rust
conditions.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on top of the leaf with powdery orange-yellow patches underneath, starting on lower leaves; infected leaves drop and branches go bare.
look_for: Orange-yellow powder under the leaf?
Pale yellow spots on top?
management: Plant resistant varieties.
Windbreak and shade trees can reduce the spores reaching the plants.
Copper fungicides are among the most effective and affordable controls.

conditions.name: Gray leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular tan to gray spots with straight edges that run between the leaf veins; leaves can be completely blighted.
look_for: Long rectangular gray spots with straight edges?
Spots limited by the leaf veins?
management: Plant resistant hybrids.
Rotate away from corn and plow residue under.

sources.title: Cercospora leaf spot (Gray leaf spot) (corn maize)

conditions.name: Northern leaf blight
conditions.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped gray-green spots that turn pale gray to tan; the spots are not limited by the veins and may look dirty from dark spores.
look_for: Long cigar-shaped gray spots?
Spots crossing the leaf veins?
management: Grow resistant varieties.
Rotate with non-host crops and manage crop debris.

conditions.name: Common rust
conditions.symptoms: Oval cinnamon-brown pustules on both sides of the leaf that release powdery reddish spores and turn dark with age.
look_for: Raised cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf sides?
Rusty powder that rubs off on your finger?
management: Plant resistant hybrids, the most effective control.
Fungicides help most when there are only a few pustules per leaf.

conditions.name: Common smut
conditions.symptoms: Swollen white to silvery galls on ears, tassels, stalks or leaves that fill with black powdery spores.
look_for: Swollen whitish galls (tumors) on the ear or tassel?
Black powder inside the galls?
management: Grow resistant or tolerant varieties and plant clean seed.
Rotate with non-cereal crops and plow deep to bury spores.
Cut out and destroy galls before they burst; do not feed infected material to livestock.

sources.title: Common smut (Boil smut, Blister smut) (corn maize)

conditions.name: Angular leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that spread between the veins and become angular; in humid weather they ooze a milky liquid that dries into a white crust. Spot centers may fall out, leaving holes.
look_for: Angular spots limited by the veins?
White crust or holes in the spots?
management: Use disease-free seed and resistant varieties.
Do not plant where cucurbits grew in the last two years.

conditions.name: Bacterial wilt
conditions.symptoms: Single runners or whole plants wilt and die quickly while leaves are still dark green. Spread by cucumber beetles.
look_for: Sudden wilting of whole runners?
Cucumber beetles on the plants?
management: Control cucumber beetles; hand-pick and destroy adults.

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.name_note: GBIF lists it as a synonym of P. fusca; recent literature treats P. xanthii as the cucurbit powdery mildew. Expert check advised.
conditions.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves, stems and fruit that spread until they cover whole leaves, which yellow and drop.
look_for: White powder that can be wiped off?
Leaves yellowing under the powder?
management: Grow resistant varieties.

conditions.name: Cercospora leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small round yellowish spots on lower leaves that develop brown centers and sometimes rings; badly affected leaves dry, curl and drop.
look_for: Round spots with brown centers starting on lower leaves?
Leaves curling and dropping?
management: Water in the morning, at the base of plants.
Space plants to lower humidity.

conditions.name: Phomopsis blight and fruit rot
conditions.symptoms: Pale sunken oval spots on the fruit that grow and merge until they cover the fruit; leaves get round brown spots with light centers and stems may have dark cankers.
look_for: Pale sunken spots on the fruit?
Round brown leaf spots with light centers?
management: Destroy infected plant material.
Plant only disease-free seed and clean transplants.

conditions.name: Phytophthora blight
conditions.symptoms: Plants wilt and die; roots and the stem at the soil line are brown and water-soaked.
look_for: Sudden wilting even when soil is wet?
Dark water-soaked stem at the soil line?
management: Plant in well-drained soil and avoid too much irrigation.
Rotate away from susceptible crops for two years.

conditions.name: Leaf blight
conditions.symptoms: Oval tan to brown spots on older leaves, often with yellow streaks running along the leaf; spots merge until leaves die back.
look_for: Tan-brown oval spots with yellow streaks?
Mostly on older leaves?
management: Check older leaves weekly.
Rotate out of onion-family crops for several years and bury crop debris.

conditions.name: Rust
conditions.symptoms: Small white flecks that become round or long orange pustules on leaves and stems; badly infected leaves yellow and die.
look_for: Orange pustules on the leaves?
Orange powder that rubs off?
management: Use only disease-free planting cloves.
Plant in well-drained soil and control weeds.

conditions.name: Leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small oval water-soaked spots on young leaves that develop white centers, dark borders and yellow halos; spots merge and leaves dry up.
look_for: Spots with white centers and dark borders?
Yellow halo around the spots?
management: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Grow the crop under partial shade.
Mulch to reduce soil splash.

sources.title: Ginger diseases: leaf spot
sources.publisher: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Agritech Portal

conditions.name: Sheath blight
conditions.symptoms: Gray-green water-soaked spots on the leaf sheaths and pseudostem that develop pale centers and brown edges.
look_for: Water-soaked spots on the leaf sheath?
Spots with pale centers and brown edges?
management: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer.
Clear old crop debris and keep the field well drained.
conditions.review_note: No ginger-specific expert source was found; this record uses guidance for the same fungus (Rhizoctonia solani) on rice and needs review by a plant pathologist.

conditions.name: Black rot
conditions.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with tiny black dots; berries get light spots, then harden, shrivel and turn black but stay on the vine.
look_for: Brown leaf spots with tiny black dots?
Hard, black, shriveled berries on the bunch?
management: Remove all mummified fruit during pruning.
Cultivate soil at bud break to bury fallen mummies.

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.gbif: Plasmopara viticola (Berk. & M.A.Curtis) Berl. & De Toni
conditions.symptoms: Shiny yellow 'oil spots' on the upper leaf with white cottony growth underneath; young berries turn grayish when infected. Favored by wet weather.
look_for: Yellow oily-looking spots on top of the leaf?
White cottony growth under the same spots?
management: Choose resistant varieties where possible.
Protect leaves and flowers during wet periods and avoid excess irrigation.

conditions.name: Esca (black measles)
conditions.gbif: Phaeomoniella chlamydospora (W.Gams, Crous, M.J.Wingf. & Mugnai) Crous & W.Gams
conditions.symptoms: 'Tiger stripe' leaves: yellow or red stripes between the veins that dry and turn brown; berries get dark spots. Cut trunks show dark streaks in the wood.
look_for: Yellow or red stripes between the leaf veins?
Dark streaks in the wood when cut?
management: There is no effective cure.
Remove and destroy infected parts.
Protect pruning wounds.

conditions.name: Leaf blight (Isariopsis leaf spot)
conditions.symptoms: Irregular dull red to brown spots 2-25 mm across that turn black and can merge.
look_for: Irregular dark brown to black spots?
Spots merging into large dead areas?
management: Sprays used for other grape diseases usually also reduce this one.

conditions.name: Leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Irregular brown to black spots on grape leaves; several fungi cause similar leaf spots.
look_for: Irregular dark spots on the leaves?
Spots merging into large dead areas?
management: Remove fallen leaves and keep the canopy open.
Sprays used for other grape diseases usually also reduce leaf spots.
conditions.review_note: PlantSeg groups several grape leaf spots under one label; this record uses Isariopsis leaf spot information and needs review.

conditions.name: Leafroll disease
conditions.symptoms: Leaves roll downward and turn red (red varieties) or yellow (white varieties) while main veins stay green; fruit ripens poorly. Spread by mealybugs and infected planting material.
look_for: Leaves rolled downward?
Red or yellow leaves with green main veins?
management: There is no cure; plant virus-tested vines.
Remove infected vines and control mealybugs.
Confirm with a laboratory test, since symptoms look like stress.

sources.title: Grapevine leafroll
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.symptoms: Light green to yellow angular patches on top of the leaf with fluffy white growth underneath.
look_for: Fluffy white growth under the leaf?
Angular yellow patches on top?
management: Plant resistant varieties.

conditions.name: Lettuce mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Young plants are stunted and deformed, sometimes with mottling; head lettuce infected early may not form heads. Spread by seed and aphids.
look_for: Stunted, deformed plants?
Mottled or yellowed, twisted leaves?
management: Plant tested, virus-free seed and resistant varieties.
Control weeds and plow under harvested lettuce fields promptly.

sources.title: Lettuce Pest Management Guidelines: Lettuce mosaic
sources.publisher: University of California Statewide IPM Program

conditions.name: Tar spot
conditions.symptoms: Yellow-green spots in early summer that become raised, shiny black tar-like spots by late summer. Mostly cosmetic.
look_for: Raised shiny black spots like tar?
Yellow halo around young spots?
management: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
conditions.symptoms: Ripe fruit gets round, sunken tan spots with rings that ooze orange or salmon spores in wet weather.
look_for: Round sunken spots with rings on ripe fruit?
Orange or salmon-colored spore ooze?
management: Remove infected fruit and diseased twigs.
Prune, thin and space trees for air flow.

conditions.name: Bacterial spot
conditions.symptoms: Angular gray water-soaked spots under the leaf that turn purple and fall out, leaving shot holes; heavily spotted leaves yellow and drop. Twigs get cankers.
look_for: Small holes where spots fell out (shot holes)?
Spots limited by the leaf veins?
management: Avoid susceptible varieties where the disease is known.
Protective copper sprays can help, but peach is sensitive to copper.

conditions.name: Brown rot
conditions.symptoms: Fruit gets a fast-spreading brown rot with gray-brown spore tufts; blossoms collapse and twigs get tan cankers.
look_for: Brown rot with gray-brown powdery tufts on the fruit?
Collapsed blossoms or twig cankers?
management: Remove mummified fruit.
Avoid sprinkler irrigation that wets flowers and fruit.

conditions.name: Peach leaf curl
conditions.symptoms: Young leaves in spring develop thick, puckered red or yellow patches and curl; a white coating may form before leaves drop.
look_for: Thick, puckered, reddish young leaves?
Leaves curling in spring?
management: Plant less susceptible varieties; none is fully resistant.

conditions.name: Rust
conditions.symptoms: Angular pale yellow-green spots on both leaf sides that turn bright yellow, with orange-red spores underneath.
look_for: Angular yellow spots on the leaves?
Orange-red powder under the leaf?
management: Protect trees in areas with early-season outbreaks.

conditions.name: Peach scab
conditions.symptoms: Small olive-green spots on the fruit near the stem end that darken and may crack the skin; twigs get small brown lesions.
look_for: Small olive-green to dark spots near the stem end of the fruit?
Cracked fruit skin?
management: Prune the canopy for air flow and light.

conditions.name: Bacterial spot
conditions.symptoms: Angular gray water-soaked spots under the leaf that turn purple and fall out, leaving shot holes; twigs get cankers.
look_for: Small holes where spots fell out (shot holes)?
Spots limited by the leaf veins?
management: Avoid susceptible varieties where the disease is known.
Protective copper sprays can help prevent infection.

conditions.name: Brown rot
conditions.symptoms: Blossoms and twigs die back; fruit gets a fast-spreading brown rot and often stays on the tree; brown spore masses form in humid weather.
look_for: Brown rotting fruit hanging on the tree?
Dead blossoms and twig cankers?
management: Remove mummified fruit.
Avoid sprinkler irrigation that wets flowers and fruit.

conditions.name: Plum pocket
conditions.name_note: Taphrina pruni in Europe; Taphrina communis in North America.
conditions.symptoms: Fruit swells into a hollow, spongy, distorted bladder up to ten times normal size, then turns brown or black and falls.
look_for: Swollen, hollow, bladder-like fruit?
No seed inside the fruit?
management: Remove infected fruit before spores form.
Plant resistant cultivars.
If fruit has been lost for several years, protect trees before bud break.

sources.title: Peach Leaf Curl and Plum Pocket

conditions.name: Plum pox (sharka)
conditions.symptoms: Yellow or brown rings, bands and vein clearing on spring leaves; fruit can be deformed with brown flesh and drop early. Some trees show no symptoms.
look_for: Yellow rings or bands on the leaves?
Deformed fruit with brown flesh?
management: Infected trees cannot be cured; report suspected cases.
Use certified planting material; confirm with a laboratory test.

conditions.name: Rust
conditions.symptoms: Angular pale yellow-green spots on both leaf sides that turn bright yellow, with orange-red spores underneath.
look_for: Angular yellow spots on the leaves?
Orange-red powder under the leaf?
management: Protect trees in areas with early-season outbreaks.

conditions.name: Early blight
conditions.symptoms: Dark spots with a yellow border and rings of raised and sunken tissue (a target pattern), first on older leaves; dead leaves stay on the plant. Tubers can get dark, dry, corky spots.
look_for: Rings inside the spots, like a target?
Started on the oldest leaves?
management: Keep plants well fed and watered to reduce stress.
Rotate crops and remove volunteer potato and tomato plants.
Store tubers in a cool place.

conditions.name: Late blight
conditions.symptoms: Pale or dark green spots with yellow halos that quickly grow into large brown-black patches, with white cottony growth at the edges under the leaf in moist weather. Stems blacken and whole plants collapse.
look_for: White cottony growth at the edge of spots under the leaf?
Patches spreading very fast in cool, wet weather?
management: Plant disease-free seed tubers and tolerant varieties.
Destroy infected tubers, leftover plants and volunteers.
Do not plant near tomato or pepper with late blight.
Inspect fields every other day after emergence; water early so leaves dry during the day.

conditions.name: Fire blight
conditions.symptoms: Cane tips blacken, bend over like a shepherd's crook and die; leaf veins blacken and berries stay brown and hard.
look_for: Blackened cane tips bent like a hook?
Creamy ooze on canes in humid weather?
management: Use healthy planting material.
Remove and burn infected parts.

conditions.name: Gray mold
conditions.symptoms: Blossoms brown and dry; berries get soft light-brown areas that spread quickly and become covered in gray powdery mold.
look_for: Gray fuzzy mold on the berries?
Soft brown rotting fruit?
management: Plant in full sun with good drainage and avoid over-fertilizing.
Harvest often, in dry weather, and remove diseased berries.
Remove fruiting canes right after harvest.

conditions.name: Leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Small dark green round spots on young leaves that turn tan to gray; the dead tissue may fall out and leaves drop early.
look_for: Small tan-gray round spots?
Holes where spots fell out?
management: Remove and burn infected debris.
Prune for good air flow.

conditions.name: Yellow rust
conditions.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules on the underside of leaves; leaves die early.
look_for: Yellow-orange pustules under the leaf?
Orange powder that rubs off?
management: Prune to improve air flow.
Growing under tunnels greatly reduces the disease.

conditions.name: Rice blast
conditions.symptoms: Diamond-shaped spots with gray or white centers and brown borders on leaves; the panicle neck can rot and break, leaving white, empty heads.
look_for: Diamond-shaped spots with gray centers?
Rotten or broken panicle necks with whitish heads?
management: Plant resistant varieties.
Avoid too much nitrogen fertilizer.
Keep good water management so plants are not drought-stressed.
Destroy infected crop residue before planting.

conditions.name: Sheath blight
conditions.symptoms: Oval green-gray water-soaked spots on the leaf sheath near the water line that develop pale centers and purple-brown edges; white cottony growth and small round brown bodies (sclerotia) may appear.
look_for: Spots on the sheath near the water line?
White cottony growth or small round brown bodies?
management: Clear plant debris from the previous harvest and keep fields well drained.
Use tolerant varieties and avoid excess nitrogen.
Scout from about 30 days after transplanting; act if about 5% of plants show symptoms.

conditions.name: Bacterial blight
conditions.name_note: Pathovar name used in plant pathology; GBIF does not list pathovars separately.
conditions.symptoms: Water-soaked spots with yellow halos that turn dark and merge, giving leaves a burned look; dead leaves stay on the plant.
look_for: Small dark spots with yellow halos?
Leaves looking burned or torn?
management: Plant certified seed and resistant varieties.

conditions.name: Brown spot
conditions.symptoms: Red-purple angular spots on both sides of the leaves, starting low on the plant, that merge into brown patches; leaves yellow and drop.
look_for: Small angular red-brown spots?
Starting on the lower leaves?
management: Plow residue under after harvest.
Rotate away from soybean for at least a year and use less susceptible varieties.

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.symptoms: Yellow or pale green spots on the upper leaf that turn gray-brown with a yellow edge, with gray-purple fuzzy tufts underneath.
look_for: Gray-purple fuzzy tufts under the leaf?
Pale yellow spots on top?
management: Use resistant varieties and treated seed.
Plow residue under and rotate away from soybean for a year.

conditions.name: Frogeye leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Angular gray spots with purple to red-brown borders, like a frog's eye.
look_for: Gray spots with dark purple-brown borders?
Dark specks in the center of the spots?
management: Plant good-quality seed and resistant varieties.
Rotate away from soybean for two years.

conditions.name: Soybean mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Mottled, puckered or deformed leaves and stunted plants, most visible in cool weather; symptoms can fade in hot weather. Seeds may have mottled coats.
look_for: Light and dark green mottling with puckered leaves?
Symptoms clearer in cool weather?
management: Use virus-free seed, the main control.
Spraying aphids does not reliably stop the virus.
Confirm with a laboratory test, since symptoms vary.

conditions.name: Soybean rust
conditions.symptoms: Small gray to red-brown spots, mostly under the leaf, with tiny volcano-shaped pustules; leaves yellow and drop early.
look_for: Tiny raised pustules under the leaf?
Leaves yellowing and dropping early?
management: Plant resistant varieties.

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.name_note: GBIF lists it as a synonym of P. fusca; recent literature treats P. xanthii as the cucurbit powdery mildew. Expert check advised.
conditions.symptoms: White powdery growth on the upper side of leaves and on stems; affected parts are stunted and distorted.
look_for: White powder that can be wiped off?
Mostly on the upper leaf surface?
management: Plant in sunny sites with good air flow and do not crowd plants.
Clean tools and equipment regularly.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
conditions.symptoms: Round black or gray leaf spots; dark sunken lesions on runners and stems; young leaves wilt in the afternoon when the crown is infected (red-brown inside).
look_for: Dark sunken lesions on runners or leaf stalks?
Red-brown discoloration inside the crown?
management: Plant only disease-free transplants and wash soil from crowns.
Rotate crops, weed regularly and avoid excess nitrogen.

conditions.name: Leaf scorch
conditions.symptoms: Many small irregular dark purple blotches that merge until the leaf looks burned; flowers and fruit stalks can also be affected.
look_for: Many small dark purple blotches?
Leaves look scorched or burned?
management: Plant resistant varieties and renew plantings regularly.
Plant in full sun with good air flow and drainage; remove old foliage at harvest.

conditions.name: Blue mold
conditions.name_note: Some authors treat it as P. hyoscyami f. sp. tabacina (GBIF follows this).
conditions.symptoms: Patches of yellowing seedlings with cupped leaves; yellow spots on leaves with fluffy blue-gray spores underneath.
look_for: Blue-gray fuzzy growth under the leaves?
Patches of yellow, cupped seedlings?
management: Avoid over-fertilizing and overhead irrigation.

conditions.name: Brown spot
conditions.symptoms: Small round target-like spots with bright yellow halos on lower leaves; spot centers dry and drop out, giving a ragged look.
look_for: Target-like spots with bright yellow halos?
Starting on the lower leaves?
management: Rotate away from tobacco and destroy stalks and roots after harvest.
Control soil nematodes and keep potassium adequate.

conditions.name: Frogeye leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Round brown spots 2-15 mm with gray centers, like a frog's eye, starting on lower leaves and moving up; black dots may appear in the centers.
look_for: Round spots with gray centers and brown borders?
Spreading from lower to upper leaves?
management: Remove and burn infected leaves.
Rotate crops, control weeds and avoid dense planting.

conditions.name: Tobacco mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patches on the leaves, which may brown and dry.
look_for: Patchy light- and dark-green mosaic?
Distorted young leaves?
management: Plant resistant varieties and remove infected plants.
Disinfect tools; wash hands after using tobacco products before touching plants.

conditions.name: Bacterial spot
conditions.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark and greasy-looking and may merge into dead patches; spot centers can dry and fall out. Fruit can also be spotted.
look_for: Small dark spots that look greasy or water-soaked?
Spot centers dried out or falling out, leaving holes?
management: Plant only certified seed and healthy transplants.
Water at the base of plants instead of using sprinklers.
Remove crop debris after harvest and rotate crops.

conditions.name: Early blight
conditions.symptoms: Brown to black spots with rings inside (like a target), often with a yellow area around them, starting on the older, lower leaves. Badly infected leaves collapse and fruit may drop early.
look_for: Rings inside the spots, like a target?
Started on the oldest, lowest leaves?
management: Rotate with non-tomato crops such as onion, beans or corn for at least two seasons.
Use certified seed and clean seedlings, and keep the nursery away from old tomato fields.
Stake, prune and space plants for air flow; avoid overhead watering.
Check plants weekly, especially leaf undersides; act early if wet weather is coming.

conditions.name: Late blight
conditions.symptoms: Water-soaked patches that quickly turn brown-black, with white fluffy growth on leaf undersides in wet weather. Stems blacken, fruit gets greasy brown blotches, and whole plants can die within days.
look_for: White fuzzy growth under the leaves in wet weather?
Large dark patches that spread very fast?
management: Check plants three times a week in wet weather and act immediately.
Do not plant next to infected tomato, potato or pepper fields; rotate with beans, corn, onion or sweet potato.
Use certified seed, disease-free seedlings and tolerant varieties.
Remove and destroy infected plants.

conditions.name: Leaf mold
conditions.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on the upper side of older leaves with olive-green to brown velvety growth underneath. Leaves wither but stay on the plant. Common in humid greenhouses.
look_for: Velvety olive or brown growth under the leaves?
Yellow patches on top of the same leaves?
management: Grow resistant varieties.
Space plants and ventilate to lower humidity; avoid wetting the leaves.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris.

conditions.name: Tomato mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling (mosaic) on leaves, sometimes yellow; young leaves may be small or distorted and fruit may have yellow blotches.
look_for: Patchy light- and dark-green mottling on the leaves?
New leaves small, twisted or fern-like?
management: Plant resistant varieties and use heat-treated seed.
Remove and destroy infected plants.
Rotate for two years away from pepper, eggplant, cucurbits and tobacco.
Disinfect tools and equipment when moving from infected areas.

conditions.name: Septoria leaf spot
conditions.symptoms: Many small round spots with gray centers and dark borders, starting on older lower leaves; tiny black dots can be seen in the spot centers.
look_for: Many small round spots with gray centers?
Tiny black dots inside the spots?
management: Remove and destroy tomato debris after harvest.
Avoid overhead watering and stake plants for air flow.
Plant disease-free material.

conditions.name: Two-spotted spider mite
conditions.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling (stippling) on leaves that later look bronzed; fine webbing and tiny moving dots on leaf undersides. Worse in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
look_for: Fine webbing on the leaves?
Tiny moving dots under the leaves?
management: Spray plants with a strong jet of water to knock mites off.
Use insecticidal soap if mites build up.
Avoid broad insecticides that kill the mites' natural enemies.

conditions.name: Target spot
conditions.symptoms: Pinpoint water-soaked spots that grow into brown spots with clear rings, dark edges and light centers; fruit gets sunken, pitted spots.
look_for: Brown spots with clear rings and light centers?
Sunken pits on the fruit?
management: Remove and destroy plant debris.
Avoid too much nitrogen fertilizer.

conditions.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl
conditions.symptoms: Small leaves that curl upward with yellow edges and veins; plants become stunted, bushy and upright, and flowers drop. Spread by whiteflies.
look_for: Leaves curled upward with yellow edges?
Whiteflies on the plants?
management: Grow resistant varieties and transplant only virus- and whitefly-free seedlings.
Pull out and destroy infected plants.
Keep fields weed-free and use yellow sticky traps to monitor whiteflies.

conditions.name: Bacterial leaf streak (black chaff)
conditions.symptoms: Water-soaked light-brown streaks on upper leaves that dry into dead stripes; black stripes on the glumes (black chaff).
look_for: Long brown streaks on the upper leaves?
Black stripes on the glumes of the head?
management: Do not plant seed from infected fields.
Avoid overhead irrigation and plant less susceptible varieties.

sources.title: Bacterial leaf streak and black chaff (wheat)

conditions.name: Head scab (Fusarium head blight)
conditions.symptoms: Spikelets turn bleached, light straw or white during flowering; kernels shrivel and discolor, and pink or dark purple-black bodies may form on the spike.
look_for: Bleached spikelets in an otherwise green head?
Shriveled, discolored kernels?
management: Plant certified clean seed and tolerant varieties.
Rotate with legumes and choose well-drained sites.
Scout at flowering when humidity is high.

conditions.name: Leaf rust
conditions.name_note: GBIF lumps it into P. recondita; wheat literature uses P. triticina for leaf rust.
conditions.symptoms: Small round orange-brown pustules scattered on the leaf blades and sheaths; spores rub off on your finger. Pustules turn dark near maturity.
look_for: Small scattered orange-brown pustules?
Orange powder that rubs off on your finger?
management: Plant resistant varieties, the best control; check current ratings, since resistance can break down.
Remove volunteer wheat and crop debris.
Avoid very early sowing and excess nitrogen.

sources.title: Identification and Control of Leaf Rust of Wheat in Georgia (C 1060)

conditions.name: Loose smut
conditions.symptoms: At heading, the spikelets are replaced by black, sooty spore masses and no grain forms.
look_for: Black, sooty heads instead of grain?
Only some heads in the field affected?
management: Plant certified, treated seed; the fungus lives inside the seed.
Grow resistant cultivars.

sources.title: Loose Smut and Common Bunt of Wheat (G1978)

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.name_note: Forma specialis of Blumeria graminis.
conditions.symptoms: White cottony patches on the upper side of lower leaves that turn gray-brown, later with black specks; fields can look yellowish.
look_for: White cottony patches on the leaves?
Mostly on the lower leaves at first?
management: Plant resistant varieties.
Avoid heavy nitrogen and very high seeding rates that make dense canopies.

conditions.name: Septoria tritici blotch
conditions.gbif: Zymoseptoria tritici (Roberge ex Desm.) Quaedvl. & Crous
conditions.symptoms: Pale gray to dark brown blotches on leaves with tiny black dots inside, starting on the lower leaves.
look_for: Brown blotches with tiny black dots?
Starting on the lower leaves?
management: Plant tolerant varieties and disease-free seed.
Rotate with legumes for at least a year and plow deep before planting.

conditions.name: Stem rust
conditions.name_note: Forma specialis of Puccinia graminis.
conditions.gbif: Puccinia graminis subsp. tritici A.L.Guyot, Massenot & Saccas, 1946
conditions.symptoms: Reddish-brown, powdery, elongated blister-like pustules on stems, leaves and glumes; they turn black late in the season.
look_for: Long reddish-brown pustules on the stems?
Pustules that break through both leaf sides?
management: Plant resistant varieties and certified seed; plant early.
Remove volunteer wheat and grass weeds that host the rust.
Inspect every 7-10 days from flag leaf to grain fill.

conditions.name: Stripe rust
conditions.name_note: Forma specialis of Puccinia striiformis.
conditions.symptoms: Yellow stripes of powdery spores (like turmeric powder) running along the leaves, especially the flag leaf.
look_for: Yellow powdery stripes along the leaf?
Powder that rubs off like turmeric?
management: Sow resistant varieties on time and use balanced fertilizer.
Monitor closely during dewy weather and in waterlogged areas.

conditions.name: Bacterial wilt
conditions.symptoms: Vines wilt badly and die quickly while leaves stay dark green; dark streaks may appear on leaves and stems. Spread by cucumber beetles.
look_for: Sudden severe wilting of vines?
Cucumber beetles on the plants?
management: Control cucumber beetles; hand-pick and destroy adults.

conditions.name: Downy mildew
conditions.symptoms: Small yellow areas on the upper leaf that become brown patches with irregular edges, with gray mold underneath.
look_for: Gray mold under the leaf?
Yellow-brown patches on top?
management: Do not crowd plants.
Water at the base of plants, not over the leaves.

sources.title: Downy mildew in cucurbitacea of cucurbit crops-India

conditions.name: Powdery mildew
conditions.name_note: GBIF lists it as a synonym of P. fusca; recent literature treats P. xanthii as the cucurbit powdery mildew. Expert check advised.
conditions.symptoms: White powdery growth on the upper side of leaves and on stems; affected parts are stunted and distorted.
look_for: White powder that can be wiped off?
Mostly on the upper leaf surface?
management: Plant in sunny sites with good air flow and do not crowd plants.
Clean tools and equipment regularly.

conditions.name: Zucchini yellow mosaic
conditions.symptoms: Plants are badly stunted; leaves show yellow mosaic, blistering and deformation, and fruits are misshapen. Spread by aphids.
look_for: Yellow mosaic and blistered leaves?
Knobby, misshapen fruit?
management: Use resistant varieties, the most effective control.
Aphid sprays rarely stop the virus.

note: Summaries were written from the cited expert sources and have not yet been reviewed by a plant pathologist.
